logline: A top student with no physical power uses physics, precision, and cold logic to survive a school hierarchy built on violence, forming unexpected alliances along the way.

bollymeter.basis: 80 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 5 critics; 93 percent audience score; Forbes singled out the nuanced acting and bullying-cycle realism; won Best OTT Original at Asia Contents Awards 2023 and Best New Actor for Park Ji-hoon at Blue Dragon Series Awards.

pull_quotes.text: Offers plenty of surprises and interesting character development. Intense, fast-paced and well-acted.

seasons.review_body: All 8 episodes dropped simultaneously on Wavve on November 18, 2022, hitting number one on the platform's paid subscriber chart within the first day and holding the top OTT topic discussion position for four consecutive weeks. The 80-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from five critics centred on one consistent observation: the show refuses the revenge-fantasy comfort its premise could easily supply. Telegraph India gave it 4.5 out of 5, noting it shows flawed characters who get caught up in the very cycle they are trying to break. Forbes praised the acting as intense and surprising. Park Ji-hoon's performance dismantled his idol-drama image and earned him Best New Actor at the Blue Dragon Series Awards. The 8-episode format is efficiently paced - no filler arcs - and each episode escalates the social stakes without becoming cartoonish.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the show's central question: what does survival look like for someone who refuses to win on violence's own terms? Yeon Si-eun is introduced as a model student who is also a precise, calculating fighter when he has no choice. Episode 1 scores among the highest-rated in the series on IMDb, a signal that the hook lands clean.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Si-eun's first confrontation - using geometry and leverage where brute force would have lost - that tells the audience exactly what kind of show this will be.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 8
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale does not offer clean resolution - the violence cycle, as critics noted, does not simply stop - but it earns its emotional payoff through what the friendships have cost. Audiences praised the finale as consistent with the show's refusal to let genre convention override psychological truth.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The cost of the alliances Si-eun formed made visible in a final sequence that critics found unexpectedly affecting.
